implementation_notes: Swift has default parameter values on every function and initializer and named arguments at every call site, so optional settings are declared in the initializer and only overridden settings appear at the call site - no option functions or builder are needed. For structs, default property values are synthesized into the memberwise initializer's defaults (SE-0242, Swift 5.1+), removing the boilerplate of restating defaults; note that the memberwise initializer is only internal, so a public struct still needs an explicit public init, and a `let` property with a default cannot be overridden through the synthesized initializer. A builder or result-builder DSL is justified only when construction must be staged or validated across fields.
pitfalls: The synthesized memberwise initializer is internal: a public struct exposes no way to construct it, so library types must write an explicit public init - typically with the same default parameter values.
A `let` stored property with an initial value does not participate as an overridable memberwise parameter, so callers cannot change it without an explicit initializer (use `var` or write the init).

Default values on less-accessible properties leak into the synthesized initializer's access level: before the Swift 6.4 change, a private stored property with a default value forced the whole memberwise init to be private, causing 'no accessible initializer' errors.

variants.name: Memberwise initializer with default property values (Swift 5.1)
variants.idiom_name: struct ServerConfig { var port = 8080 } -> init(port: Int = 8080)
variants.implementation_notes: Give each stored property its default value and let the compiler synthesize the memberwise initializer with matching default arguments (SE-0242), so construction reads `ServerConfig(port: 9000)` and the defaults live in one place - the property declaration. This is the concise Swift realization of 'defaults plus named overrides'; it requires Swift 5.1+, applies to structs only, and cannot be exposed publicly, so public API types fall back to an explicit initializer with default parameter values.
variants.code_sketch:
struct ServerConfig {
  var host = "localhost"
  var port = 8080
  var tls = false
}

let cfg = ServerConfig(port: 9000)      // other defaults from properties
let secure = ServerConfig(tls: true)    // any subset, any order
pitfalls: The memberwise initializer is internal and is not generated when the struct declares any custom initializer (write custom inits in an extension to keep it).
`let` properties with initial values are not overridable through the synthesized init, so a configuration whose fields must be immutable needs an explicit initializer.
Property-order changes silently change the synthesized parameter order; named arguments keep call sites working, but positional callers break.
